invariants: one session mode is active and a later authorized entry tears down its predecessor
closed or replaced registry authority retires the active mode synchronously and retained controls become inert
enter and exit lifecycle callbacks cannot change keyboard ownership
failed entry tears down once and permits a later healthy entry
a key callback may install a replacement and its predecessor exit result normalizes to handled
host exit clears activation identity before lifecycle work and deferred old controls remain inert
old activation scopes cannot inspect or exit a same-extension replacement
same-registry content updates preserve activation while registry identity replacement exits it
unmount exits once and permanently closes retained controls
throwing key handlers are contained and retire through the controller

nativeAdaptation.controls: JSON-RPC actions replace retained JavaScript control closures. Each key-response batch carries its activation identity; ordinary command actions are unscoped and lifecycle ownership actions are inert.
nativeAdaptation.lifecycle: The Ratatui host clears ownership before exit callbacks, invokes exit after failed entry, and runs teardown during review-app drop.
nativeAdaptation.replacement: Monotonic activation IDs preserve the source object-identity contract even when a mode replaces itself with the same extension and mode IDs.
nativeAdaptation.coverage: Ten Rust controller behavior tests translate all ten upstream tests; Ratatui and compiled Vim-extension tests exercise action filtering, routing, Escape, reload, status, and teardown integration.
